angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 5,764,570 km at 42.75 pc = 1.8 mas. The record's radius is the volume-equivalent sphere of the fit's two radii; the fit gives the radii, not one diameter.
distanceSource: Kervella et al. (2022), A&A 667, A111, Table 4: the Hipparcos parallax 23.39 +/- 0.57 mas (van Leeuwen 2007) the orbit is scaled with, inverted (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202244009): 42.753 +/- 1.042 pc; Gaia DR3 cannot see the star
radiusSource: Radius 8.286 solar radii from Domiciano de Souza et al. (2014), A&A 569, A10, Table 6: equatorial radius 9.16 +/- 0.23 and polar radius 6.78 solar radii, from the Roche-von Zeipel fit to VLTI/PIONIER data; the record holds the volume-equivalent sphere of the two, 8.286 solar radii, and the scene draws the flattening (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/201424144): 5,764,570 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 5.99 +/- 0.6 solar masses from Kervella et al. (2022), A&A 667, A111, Table 4: mass of A 5.99 +/- 0.60 solar masses, the orbit's total mass less B's model mass (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202244009); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 15539 +/- 438 K from Kervella et al. (2022), A&A 667, A111, Table 4: Teff of A 15539 +/- 438 K (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202244009). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/achernar.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 3.379, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: SIMBAD, * alf Eri: spectral type B6Vpe (2006MNRAS.371..252L)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: SIMBAD, * alf Eri: projected rotation speed 235 km/s, the measurement SIMBAD prefers (2005yCat.3244....0G)

shape.qualification: A Roche surface flattened by rotation, 9.16 solar radii at the equator and 6.78 at the poles, its pole 60.6 degrees from the line of sight at position angle 216.9 degrees, and gravity darkened with exponent 0.166 from a 17,124 K pole: Domiciano de Souza et al. (2014), A&A 569, A10 (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/201424144). The disc color is the star's measured one; only the pole-to-equator contrast is the model's.
